newsitem.title: FRANCE: Deutsche cuts PSA Peugeot estimates.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche cuts PSA Peugeot estimates.

text.p: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell lowered its earnings estimates for French carmaker PSA Peugeot Citroen to 24 francs per share for 1997 from 39.70 francs previously.
It also cut its earnings per share (EPS) estimate for the group for 1998 to 47.70 francs from 55.50 francs.
It kept its 1996 EPS estimate unchanged at 30.10 francs.
"Despite the earnings cut, we remain neutral," Deutsche said in a stock comment distributed on Monday. "The valuation of Peugeot shares remains, together with Volkswagen, the lowest in the industry."
But, it added, "To become positive on the stock we really need signs for a 'natural' recovery of the French market and/or a serious cost-cutting programme."
The Peugeot group's new car sales fell 43 percent in France last month, compared with a fall in the market of 33.6 percent from artificially inflated January 1996 levels.

Deutsche said the Peugeot group signalled that the government had not responded yet to the French carmakers' request for assistance in funding an early retirement programme aimed at cutting staff and lowering the average age.
Shares in PSA Peugeot Citroen were down 1.21 percent at 572 francs at 1435 GMT.
